errors.commonPassword: That's one of the most commonly used passwords in the world. Anyone who copies vault.enc would guess it within seconds, however strong the encryption is. Pick another.

errors.leftoverIntact: The encrypted copy was written and verified, but the original {{name}} couldn't be removed (it may be open in another program). It still contains the real secret: close whatever is holding it and delete it yourself. Your data is safe either way; the .levault file is complete and verified.
errors.leftoverOverwritten: The encrypted copy was written and verified. The original {{name}} was overwritten with random bytes but couldn't be deleted (it may be open in another program). It no longer contains your secret; the .levault file does. Delete the leftover yourself.

errors.sidecarMismatch: {{name}} already exists and doesn't contain this file's current contents. Resolve that by hand: one of the two files isn't what you think.

encrypt.title: Confirm encrypt file
encrypt.destroyed: THE ORIGINAL FILE WILL BE DESTROYED. After the encrypted copy is written and verified, {{name}} is overwritten with random bytes and deleted. The only way back is this vault's master password or its recovery key.
encrypt.durabilityCaveat: If vault.enc on this machine is lost, this file can't be recovered. The recovery key alone isn't enough: it only works together with vault.enc. Back that file up.
encrypt.gitSafe: The .levault file is pure ciphertext and is safe to commit to git. Its filename still reveals the original filename.
encrypt.overwriteCaveat: Overwriting is best effort. On SSDs and journaling filesystems the original bytes may still exist in storage this program can't reach (wear levelling, shadow copies, backups, swap files). If this file was ever exposed, rotate the credential; don't rely on this deletion.
encrypt.resume: An encrypted copy of this file already exists and is verified to contain exactly its current contents: a previous run was interrupted before the original could be destroyed. Only the deletion below is left to do.
encrypt.unlockTitle: Unlock the vault to encrypt a file

decrypt.title: Confirm decrypt file
decrypt.warn: This writes a real secret to disk permanently and it is not cleaned up. The AI assistant can see this path and has been told not to read the file, but that isn't enforced.
decrypt.leftInPlace: The .levault file stays in place; this doesn't remove the file from the vault.
decrypt.renamed: This was encrypted as {{name}} but will be restored under the name above. The output name comes from the .levault file's name, not from what is stored inside it.
decrypt.unlockTitle: Unlock the vault to decrypt a file

abandon.confirm: These files are gone forever. Abandon them.
abandon.onlyIf: Only continue if you are certain these no longer exist anywhere:
abandon.otherwise: If any of them might still exist, cancel: make it reachable and run the rotation again instead.

recoveryKey.title: Save your recovery key
recoveryKey.written: I have written this down on paper
recoveryKey.groups: Groups of 4 characters separated by hyphens. The last group is the checksum.
recoveryKey.reentry: Re-enter the full key from your paper
recoveryKey.slot: Slot ID: {{id}}. Check that it matches any saved printout to tell whether it is stale.
recoveryKey.steps: 1. Write the full key on paper, then tick the box. 2. Re-enter the FULL key from your paper to confirm it was written correctly. Checking only a few characters proves nothing.
recoveryKey.warning: Once this page closes, the key can't be shown again. Write it down on paper and store it safely: it is the only way to regain access if you forget your master password.

recover.title: Recover access
recover.warning: Use this only if you've forgotten your master password. Your paper recovery key lets you set a new master password.

manage.title: Manage vault
manage.infoSetupRecovery: A paper recovery key lets you reset your master password if you forget it. It genuinely increases attack surface: anyone who finds the paper can reset your password. A password-only vault is also a valid and secure choice.
manage.noActions: No actions are available for this vault state.
manage.recoveryActive: Recovery slot: active · slot id: {{id}} · created: {{created}}
manage.warnReissue: This generates a new recovery key. Your old paper key stops working immediately.
manage.warnRetire: This permanently deletes every old file key from the vault. Any .levault file still encrypted under one, including copies on other machines, in backups or in git history, becomes permanently unreadable. It is refused unless every registered file has already been rotated onto the current key and is readable right now. Files this vault has never been told about can't be checked.
manage.warnRotate: Changing your master password does not change the key that protects your encrypted files. That is deliberate, and it is why a .levault committed to git keeps working. Rotate that key here if you believe it may have been exposed. Every encrypted file this machine can find ({{count}} registered) is re-encrypted under a new key. Missing files are skipped and keep working under the old key, which is retained. Nothing becomes unreadable until you separately retire the old keys.
manage.warnUpgrade: After upgrading, older versions of this plugin can no longer open the vault. An older build reports "Wrong password" for a correct password. There is no data loss, but it is alarming if you aren't expecting it. Only upgrade if all your installations are current.
